key_insight: A mixed-dimensional finite-element model lets embedded electroactive beam networks respond to the surrounding 3D electric field, enabling two-way electromechanical coupling without giving the beams their own electric-potential unknowns.
engineering_relevance: This provides a much more efficient way to simulate and homogenize dense fiber-reinforced soft dielectric composites, capturing architecture-dependent mechanical and electrical behavior without full 3D fiber meshes.
method: Geometrically exact electroactive beams are embedded in a deformable dielectric matrix.
The matrix electric field is sampled along beam centerlines and used in the beam dielectric enthalpy.
Beam-matrix mechanics are enforced with projected mortar constraints and solved monolithically.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports verification studies on discretization and field-sampling sensitivity, then applies the model to structured and irregular network examples to show architecture-dependent responses.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the sampling and constraint projection between the matrix field and beam centerlines, so coarse discretization or poor embedding could affect results.
paper_title: Mixed-Dimensional Electromechanical Coupling of Embedded Beam Networks in Soft Dielectric Composites
